head: AdGuard Home 1.0 update: new interface and per-device settings
dek: AdGuard Home, the ad and tracker blocker you install once for your whole home network, reached version 1.0 on 20 November, eight years after its first preview. It has a rebuilt interface that uses less memory and works on phones, settings for each device and a more detailed query log.
details: The query log can now be sorted and filtered, and blocklists, allowlists, DNS rewrites and your own rules sit in one Filters section with their own update times. Version 1.0 keeps the old settings file, so existing setups carry over, and new installations now use Cloudflare DNS by default instead of Quad9. AdGuard says even small updates may now bring changes that don't work with older setups. Planned next: a self-check page, mass import of filter lists, search in the interface and automatic security certificates.
where: Everyone running AdGuard Home; free and open source
means: If you run AdGuard Home on a router or a small computer, its interface now fits a phone screen and each device can get its own rules.
todo: Update from the prompt in AdGuard Home's interface (Docker users switch to the latest image); your settings stay.
